# teams agent update-endpoint

Update the messaging endpoint on an existing Agent 365 blueprint

## Usage

```
teams agent update-endpoint <endpoint> [name] [options]
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `endpoint` | HTTPS URL for the messaging endpoint | Yes |
| `name` | [OPTIONAL] Agent name. Not needed if a365.generated.config.json exists in the current directory | No |

## Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--json` | [OPTIONAL] Output as JSON |
<!-- AUTOGENERATED:END -->

## Details

Replaces the messaging endpoint registered on an existing agent blueprint — the step you need after a new devtunnel/ngrok session, or after deploying your bot to a new URL. Runs `a365 setup blueprint --update-endpoint <url>` against the blueprint identified by `[name]` or the `a365.generated.config.json` in the current directory.

### Prerequisites

- An agent identity already created with [`teams agent create`](./create)
- Logged in: `teams login`
- Signed in to the same tenant with the Azure CLI (`az login`) as with `teams login`

### Examples

Update the endpoint for the blueprint in the current directory:

```bash
teams agent update-endpoint https://your-tunnel.devtunnels.ms/api/messages
```

Update the endpoint for a specific agent by name:

```bash
teams agent update-endpoint https://your-tunnel.devtunnels.ms/api/messages "My Support Agent"
```

### Output

On success (human mode), outputs the agent blueprint ID and the new messaging endpoint. With `--json`, outputs:

```json
{
  "agentBlueprintId": "...",
  "messagingEndpoint": "https://your-tunnel.devtunnels.ms/api/messages",
  "generatedConfigPath": "/path/to/a365.generated.config.json"
}
```
